title: Pasta alla Norma
subtitle: sicilian pasta with fried aubergine, tomato and ricotta
excerpt: Pasta alla norma is a Sicilian pasta dish of fried aubergine, sharp tomato sauce with garlic and basil, topped with ricotta and a drizzle of olive oil. The aubergine is fried separately and added at the end so it keeps its texture rather than melting into the sauce. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla norma comes from Catania in Sicily and was named in honour of Vincenzo Bellini's opera Norma, which premiered in 1831. The dish is said to have been declared as magnificent as the opera by the playwright Nino Martoglio, and the name stuck. It is considered one of the defining dishes of Sicilian cooking.

glossaryTerms.definition: Referring to pasta alla norma, a Sicilian pasta dish of fried aubergine, tomato sauce and ricotta salata, named after Bellini's opera.
A firm, salted and aged form of ricotta used as a grating cheese in Sicilian and southern Italian cooking, sharper and drier than fresh ricotta.

content.text: uses a technique common to Sicilian cooking: frying the aubergine separately in plenty of hot olive oil before adding it to the sauce. This keeps the pieces distinct and tender rather than dissolving into the tomato. The
is crumbled or grated over at the end to add a salty, creamy note. Serves 4.

Fresh ricotta is used here as a substitute for the traditional ricotta salata, which can be hard to find. Spoon it over in dollops rather than spreading it so there are pockets of creaminess throughout each serving.

Heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in a frying pan over high heat. Fry the aubergine cubes in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Do not crowd the pan. Transfer to a plate lined with kitchen paper and season to taste.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and fry for 1 minute until softened but not coloured.

Add the tinned tomatoes and break them up with a spoon. Season to taste and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the oil has separated slightly to the surface. Stir in half the basil.
Cook the pasta in a large pan of boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.
Toss the pasta in the tomato sauce over low heat, adding a splash of pasta water if needed. Add the fried aubergine and toss gently to combine without breaking it up too much.
Serve in bowls with the remaining basil scattered on top and the ricotta spooned over in small dollops. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

attrs.cause: The oil was not hot enough when the aubergine was added
attrs.fix: Make sure the oil is shimmering before the aubergine goes in. Fry in small batches and drain on kitchen paper immediately

attrs.symptom: Tomato sauce is thin and watery
attrs.cause: The sauce was not simmered long enough to reduce
attrs.fix: Simmer uncovered for the full 15 minutes. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon before the pasta goes in

attrs.symptom: Aubergine loses its shape when tossed with the pasta
attrs.cause: It was overcooked in the initial fry or stirred too vigorously
attrs.fix: Fry the aubergine until golden but still holding its shape. Add it to the pasta gently at the end and fold rather than toss

content.text: Pasta alla norma comes from Catania in eastern Sicily, where it is a point of intense local pride. It is made with rigatoni or maccheroni in Catania, though short pasta with ridges is the practical rule. The traditional topping is ricotta salata, a firm salted ricotta that is grated over like a cheese. It is one of the most complete expressions of Sicilian flavour in a single bowl.
